newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek Sportsman H1 profit up 34.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Greek Sportsman H1 profit up 34.8 pct.

text.p: Greek retailer Sportsman posted a 34.8 percent increase in first half pretax earnings to 731 million drachmas compared to the same period a year earlier on turnover growth of 14.1 percent to 2.97 billion drachmas.
Management forecast 1997 pretax profit would exceed 1.15 billion drachmas, an upward revision from its April 1997 estimate of a 1.1 billion drachma profit for the year.
According to the same estimates, earnings would climb to 1.3 and 1.6 billion drachmas in 1998 and 1999, respectively.
The company had pretax earnings of 370 million drachmas on turnover of 4.74 billion in 1996.
Sportsman is the main distributor of Lacoste sportswear, footwear and cosmetics in Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Cyprus and FYROM, besides Greece.
Its subsidiary commercial company Endysi is also listed on the Athens bourse's small-cap parallel market.
Sportsman's common stock jumped to its upper daily volatility limit on Thursday, adding 168 drachmas to 2,268 with open buying interest. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
